chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the son of the adulterer, is his testimony allowed? So he (peace be upon him) said: No.
So I said, 'Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba is alleging that it is allowed'.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, do not forgive his sin'.
What Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba: 'And it is a Reminder for you and your people'.
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of the son of the adulterer accepted in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rejects the testimony of 'walad al-zina' (child of fornication), directly contradicting the jurist Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, whom he invokes with a divine curse. The Imam supports this ruling by citing Surah Az-Zukhruf, 43:44, interpreting the verse as a specific divine address or sign confirming the validity of this legal distinction for Al-Hakam and his followers.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the son of the adultery, is his testimony allowed?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
So I said, ‘Al-Hakam Bin Uteyba is alleging that it is allowed’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Do not Forgive his sin.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic did not Say to Al-Hakm Bin Uteyba [43:44] And it is a Reminder for you and your people’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Aban from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the testimony of one who is born out of wedlock if it is acceptable. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not acceptable.’
I then said that al-Hakam ibn al-‘Utaybah considers it acceptable.
He (the Imam) said, ‘O Lord, do not forgive his sin.
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has not said to al-Hakam ibn ‘Utaybah, ‘. . . it is a reminder for you and your people.’ ( 43 : 44 )”
